title: revloop address intent
description: What the address leg returns. It is intent for the orchestrator to act on, never a record of what the agent already did — the agent holds no GitHub credential and makes no GitHub call. Carries the same two harness-forced shapes as the findings schema: no $schema or $id key, because Claude Code's --json-schema rejects a schema naming the 2020-12 meta-schema; and every property listed in 'required', because Codex enforces OpenAI strict mode. Optional fields are nullable rather than absent.

blocked.description: True when the leg could not do its job at all. Terminates the loop.

blocked_reason.description: Why, or null. Only meaningful when blocked is true.

wrap_up.description: The overall comment body, in Markdown, explaining what was fixed, skipped, deferred and rebutted. Written for a collaborator who has never heard of revloop. The orchestrator appends the machine-readable marker and any 'Deferred work filed' list; do not write either yourself.

dispositions.description: One entry per finding supplied in the prompt. Every finding gets one, whatever its severity — severity governs what happens after verification, never whether verification happens.

finding_id.description: The id supplied in the prompt. Not invented here.

disposition.description: fixed: code changed. skipped: not acting by policy, such as a nit past skip_nits_after_pass. deferred: real, worth doing, not here — persists to a sink. rebutted: technically wrong for this codebase. escalated: needs a human decision, applies revloop/stop and leaves the thread open.

reply.description: The in-thread reply body to post. Always required: nothing is silently dropped, and a skipped nit still gets a one-line reason.

persist.description: For a deferred defect worth recording outside this PR, the issue to file. Null for every other disposition. Write it to stand alone for someone who never saw the PR.

title.description: One line naming the defect, as an issue title rather than a review comment.

body.description: What the defect is, where, why it matters, and what fixing it would involve. Measure before asserting: a headline number that turns out to be mostly unrelated makes the issue misleading.

duplicate_of.description: The number of an existing issue that already covers this defect, chosen from the candidates supplied in the prompt. Null when none of them match. Ambiguity counts as a match: a missed filing still has the PR thread behind it, while a duplicate is mess someone has to clean up.
